title: Consumer Class Actions
scope: United States; selected, source-linked consumer class-action settlements; not a comprehensive case database

methodology.classification: Class-action settlements only. FTC/CFPB enforcement refunds are separate remedies and never counted as class-action settlements.
methodology.claims: A proposed settlement and an open claim window are independent attributes. Claim deadlines, class eligibility, payments, final approvals, and appeals may change. Confirm against the settlement notice before taking action.
methodology.damages: Settlement fund amounts are gross figures, not per-person payouts, proven consumer losses, or admissions of liability.
sourceHierarchy: Court docket, settlement order and notice
methodology.verification: Primary-source case facts manually reviewed November 10, 2026. The directory is a set of discovery links, not an automatically synchronized feed. ClassAction.org listing dates, proceedings, claim deadlines and eligibility may change and require rechecking.
methodology.discoverySources: ClassAction.org, Top Class Actions, Consumer Action, and ClaimDepot are secondary discovery sources. They vary in mission and business model. None is treated as an official claims administrator or a replacement for the court docket.
methodology.sourceUse: Link to and attribute third-party directories; do not scrape or mirror their content, assume an API or republication license, or treat listing dates as live eligibility. Promote only independently verified court/administrator records into the verified-case explorer.

cases.caseName: Brewer et al. v. CVS Pharmacy, Inc. and Criteo Corp.
cases.court: Circuit Court of the 17th Judicial Circuit, Broward County, Florida
cases.headline: A proposed $20.5M settlement addresses allegations about third-party tracking on CVS digital properties.
cases.allegations: Plaintiffs alleged that data from visitors to CVS digital sites and apps was disclosed to technology providers without valid consent. CVS and Criteo deny wrongdoing.
cases.classSummary: People who accessed certain CVS websites or apps in the United States before July 27, 2026; exclusions and notice conditions apply.
cases.payout: Up to $5 without documentation or $10 with proof, potentially reduced; not guaranteed.
cases.action: Review the official notice and only file if the class definition fits. Claim deadline is November 16, 2026.
cases.officialEvidence: Administrator website cited by case reporting; direct automated access returned 403 on 2026-11-10. Reverify official notice before relying on terms.

cases.headline: A $250M proposed settlement covers claims about certain Siri Apple Intelligence features.
cases.allegations: Consumers alleged that eligible iPhones were purchased expecting certain advertised Siri Apple Intelligence features that allegedly were not delivered. Apple denies the allegations and any wrongdoing.
cases.classSummary: Original U.S. purchasers, not for resale, of specified iPhone 15 Pro or iPhone 16 models bought June 10, 2024–March 29, 2025; eligibility details matter.
cases.payout: Administrator describes a $25 starting amount per eligible device, adjusted pro rata up to $95 or down; not guaranteed.
cases.action: Check purchase date, model and the official notice; submit a separate claim per eligible device if qualified.
cases.officialEvidence: Settlement administrator landing page and important dates; accessed 2026-11-10.

cases.court: U.S. District Court for the District of Columbia
cases.headline: A proposed $167.5M antitrust settlement concerns surcharges at independent ATMs.
cases.allegations: Plaintiffs alleged network rules limited price competition among independent ATMs, causing higher surcharges. Defendants deny wrongdoing.
cases.classSummary: Certain U.S. ATM or PIN-debit withdrawals at independently operated ATMs from October 24, 2007 through August 14, 2026, where surcharge fees were not fully reimbursed; see official notice.
cases.payout: Unknown until claims and deductions are finalized. The fund is not a guaranteed payout to an individual.
cases.action: Review transactions and official settlement notice; eligible claims are due February 10, 2027.
cases.officialEvidence: Official settlement administrator website and notice; accessed 2026-11-10.

cases.caseName: In re Equifax Inc. Customer Data Security Breach Litigation
cases.court: U.S. District Court for the Northern District of Georgia
cases.headline: Court-approved data-breach settlement: cash claim deadlines have passed, but certain restoration assistance continues.
cases.allegations: Consumers alleged failures to adequately protect their information and delays in notifying them after the 2017 breach. Equifax denied wrongdoing; no court found wrongdoing in the settlement.
cases.classSummary: Individuals identified among approximately 147 million people affected by the 2017 breach, subject to the terms of the class settlement.
cases.payout: At least $380.5M in the consumer restitution fund; personal payments were subject to eligibility and claim volume. All initial and extended cash claim deadlines have passed.
cases.action: Do not submit a new cash claim: the extended deadline passed January 22, 2024. If affected, review identity restoration assistance available through January 2029.
cases.officialEvidence: Official settlement administrator FAQ and key dates; settlement received final approval in January 2020.

cases.caseName: Guzman et al. v. Dr. Squatch, LLC
cases.court: Superior Court of California, County of Los Angeles
cases.headline: A proposed $9M settlement concerns allegations that some 'natural' personal-care products contained synthetic ingredients.
cases.allegations: Consumers alleged that labels describing specified Dr. Squatch products as natural were misleading because certain ingredients were allegedly synthetic. Dr. Squatch denies the allegations and denies wrongdoing.
cases.classSummary: U.S. purchasers of qualifying Dr. Squatch products bearing a 'natural' label between November 1, 2018 and August 29, 2026; covered-product list and exclusions apply.
cases.payout: The court-supervised notice describes a pro rata settlement fund after fees and costs. Amounts depend on documented purchases, valid claims and court approval; not guaranteed.
cases.action: Check whether your purchases are on the covered-products list and submit a claim by November 27, 2026 if eligible.
cases.officialEvidence: Official settlement administrator notice and FAQs, reviewed 2026-11-10; preliminary settlement awaiting final court approval.

cases.caseName: Alexander Garner v. Aramark Management Services LP
cases.court: Superior Court of the District of Columbia, Civil Division
cases.headline: A proposed $4.5M settlement covers an allegedly undisclosed 3% concession venue fee.
cases.allegations: The lawsuit alleged that Aramark failed to properly disclose a 3% venue fee charged on food and beverage purchases at Capital One Arena. Aramark denies wrongdoing and liability.
cases.classSummary: People who paid the venue fee on Aramark purchases at Capital One Arena between October 1, 2024 and December 31, 2025, subject to the official notice.
cases.payout: Eligible claimants receive a pro rata share of the net fund after court-approved costs and fees. No fixed per-person payment is promised.
cases.action: Review whether your concession purchases included the 3% venue fee; file a claim by December 4, 2026 if eligible.
cases.officialEvidence: Official court-supervised settlement website and FAQs, reviewed 2026-11-10; court has not granted final approval.
